title: growth-compass-onepage-anelise
content:
Purpose: a compact, action-oriented one page I can bring to a manager check to 1) surface progress against signals, 2) ask for specific partner help, and 3) align on next 6–12 week experiments. Keep it short; use this as the meeting script and the single slide I can share in follow-ups.

Structure (what to cover in 10–12 minutes):
- 20s: Quick framing — role focus and current priority area (what I own).
- 90s: Metric signals and recent wins (data + short context).
- 2–3 min: Narrative — what changed, why it matters, and the evidence.
- 2 min: Risks, blockers, and things I’m concerned about.
- 2 min: Specific asks for manager (& one ask for leadership).
- 30s: 6–12 week experiments and a success definition.

My current framing (elevator):
- Role focus: Individual contributor on talent programs — I lead onboarding optimization experiments and the mentorship program pilot.
- Current north star: reduce time-to-first-impact for new hires (measured as % of new hires meeting onboarding milestones in first 90 days).

Signals & evidence (last 90 days):
- Quantitative signals:
  - Baseline: 56% new hires hit all onboarding milestones in 90 days (Q4 internal cohort).
  - Recent change: pilot cohort (n=18) with revised mentor pairing -> 72% milestone completion (+16 pts).
  - Engagement signal: onboarding doc completion rate + Slack intro thread responses improved by ~30% for pilot.
- Qualitative signals: new hire feedback highlights faster ramp on internal tooling but continued confusion on escalation paths (3/10 comments flagged).
- What this suggests: mentor pairing appears to move the needle on practical adoption; escalation clarity still a process gap.

Narrative (short):
- I ran two small experiments: (A) structured mentor pairing + 1:1 agenda template, (B) paired onboarding office hours twice/week. Pairing clearly improved milestone completion; office hours had modest lift in tooling questions but low attendance.
- Hypothesis: structured, time-boxed mentoring + clearer escalation docs will increase milestone completion to 80% across cohorts.

Risks & blockers:
- Capacity: mentors currently unpaid volunteers; scaling requires explicit allocation/ODR or a small stipend.
- Docs ownership: escalation and runbook pages have unclear owners — they drift. Need a single owner or rotation.
- Measurement noise: milestone tracking relies on manager self-reports; we need an automated pulse via HRIS or a short pulse survey.

Specific asks (manager):
- Short-term (this quarter): approve a 4-week mentor stipend pilot budget (estimate $2k for 20 mentors) and help prioritize an owner for the escalation runbook.
- Mid-term: help surface this pilot to one product leader to recruit senior mentors from Eng for next cohort.
- Coaching ask: help me phrase the impact case for the stipend to Finance and to create a 1-page cost/benefit that ties to ramp speed and early retention.

One ask for leadership (if asked):
- Ask for a small cross-functional forum invite (L+PM+Eng+People Ops) to align on top 3 onboarding friction points and commit a 90-day collective experiment.

6–12 week experiments (what I’ll run next):
- Experiment 1 (weeks 1–6): mentor stipend pilot + pairing rubric; measure milestone completion, mentor satisfaction, and cost per incremental completer. Success = 80% milestone completion for pilot.
- Experiment 2 (weeks 3–10): appoint runbook owner + rewrite escalation doc; measure reduction in escalation-related questions in office hours and Slack. Success = 50% drop in escalation questions.
- Experiment 3 (weeks 4–12): replace manager self-report with a 4-question pulse on day 30/60/90 to reduce measurement bias. Success = 80% response rate and clearer trendlines.

Evidence bank (snippets to paste into follow-ups):
- Pilot cohort milestone completion: 13/18 completers (72%).
- Quote: "Mentor pairing got me unstuck on build pipeline in week 2 — I shipped faster." (New hire, Data infra team).
- Slack thread: onboarding-office-hours-attendance (link: SLACK:T12345/messages/234).

Potential objections & my short scripts:
- Finance pushback on stipend: "Small stipend reduces mentor dropout and scales the program without manager heavy-lift; we’ll test ROI in 6 weeks and revert if not predictive."
- Leader bandwidth: "This is a lightweight experiment with limited time commitments per mentor (2–3hrs/month) and measurable signals to decide next steps."

Follow-up plan (after the check):
- Send 1-slide recap within 24hrs with the three asks and next steps.
- Share measurement dashboard link and raw cohort data (anonymized) within 72hrs.
- If stipend pilot approved, schedule mentor orientation + pairing by week 2.

Notes for self (things to write down before meeting):
- Bring the 1-paragraph success story and two data points (72% vs 56% + Slack engagement).
- Be explicit about the ask size (dollars, owner, time).
- Have the 90-day fallback plan if stipend is denied (rotate mentor credits, non-financial recognition).

Open questions I want to answer with manager during the check:
- Is there appetite to fund a 4-week stipend pilot?
- Who in Leadership would be the right partner to make mentor recruitment easier?
- Any known Finance constraints I should anticipate?

Quick action items to run after this doc:
- Draft the 1-page cost/benefit for Finance (deadline: 48hrs).
- Propose list of 20 mentors based on interest survey (deadline: 3 business days).
- Draft a short escalation-runbook owner role description and proposed rotation (deadline: 1 week).

Longer-term signals I care about (not in this meeting):
- Time-to-first-coding-merge, early retention at 6 months, NPS of onboarding, manager time saved per hire.

Revision log (keeps me honest):
- 2026-01-18: initial draft (metrics and experiment plan).
- 2026-01-25: added stipend estimate and tighter asks after chat with Diego.
- 2026-02-05: tightened success criteria and added pulse idea after Mira's feedback.

End notes: this doc is intentionally a short script. If it grows, carve off a one-pager for Finance and a separate pilot playbook for the mentor cohort.
